transcript: I went to my first show at BAM's Howard Gilman Opera House the other night, The Threepenny Opera. It's an almost century-old German satire about capitalism, but it feels right at home in the States in 2025. The story revolves around Macheath, a local criminal in London who's our antihero, but he's far from the only shady character. It’s basically a whole slew of plot points showcasing amorality, corruption, and sins galore, and this production by the Berliner Ensemble is just the right amount of ridiculous without losing the searing potency of the critiques on society that this play is presenting. I thought the score was fine, but I was mostly entertained by the story, the wonderfully unhinged performance by Gabriel Schneider as Macheath, and the staging which utilized a scaffolding-jungle-gym type of set. This was performed in German with English captions, but I gotta say that some of the captions seemed poorly timed, overly simplified, or just straight up missing. I got the information that I needed, but I was tired and it was a little more involved than I was hoping it would be. Also along the lines of clarity, I think I would have enjoyed this a little more in a smaller space. This was a super brief run, but I'll definitely be on the lookout for any future work by the Berliner Ensemble or other productions of the Threepenny Opera that may come through New York. With that another program for my collection.
